clearedSpotChecks.check: Jump destination analysis in revm-bytecode 10.0.0 (Celo), 11.0.1 (X Layer) and 42.0.0 (celo-kona main), including the trailing PUSH pointer fix of 42.0.0.
clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_getCode of the PoolManager on both chains returns 24,009 bytes; a linear walk that skips PUSH immediates ends exactly at offset 24,009 with the last instruction 0x0a (EXP) at 24,008 and 610 executable JUMPDESTs. In revm-bytecode-10.0.0/src/legacy/analysis.rs lines 11-60 (fetched from static.crates.io) the jump bitmap has the code length, bits are set only for JUMPDEST bytes reached as instructions, and a trailing truncated PUSH only grows zero padding, so the pointer overrun cannot mark or unmark a destination in the PoolManager's code.
